title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): Russian President Vladimir Putin “didn’t even want to take Ukraine.”
text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin “didn’t even want to take Ukraine.”
Russian experts told us that Kennedy's statement is incredulous. "He does not want to take Ukraine?" Steven Pifer, a former Ukraine ambassador, told us. "Putin clearly wants territory."

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “And that’s why they [NATO] have money today because of what I did. And then I hear that they like Obama better.
text:
“And that’s why they [NATO] have money today because of what I did. And then I hear that they like Obama better. They should like Obama better. ... Because he didn’t ask for anything."
Obama and his top aides repeatedly pressured NATO countries to increase their military spending.

claimReviewed: “And that’s why they [NATO] have money today because of what I did. And then I hear that they like Obama better. They should like Obama better. ... Because he didn’t ask for anything."

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): A proclamation by President Joe Biden to limit asylum eligibility "establishes an annual minimum of approximately 2 million illegal alien
text:
A proclamation by President Joe Biden to limit asylum eligibility "establishes an annual minimum of approximately 2 million illegal alien border crossers."
The proclamation limits asylum eligibility for those caught trying to cross the southern border illegally when the number of people apprehended reaches a daily average of 2,500 encounters or more for seven straight days.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “NATO was busted until I came along. I said everybody’s going to pay."
text:
“NATO was busted until I came along. I said everybody’s going to pay."
Even in terms of indirect spending by countries on their own defense, that was going up before Trump took office.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): The Emergency National Security Supplemental Appropriations Act “accepts 5,000 illegal immigrants a day.”
text:
The Emergency National Security Supplemental Appropriations Act “accepts 5,000 illegal immigrants a day.”
Under the proposed bill, most migrants caught crossing into the U.S. illegally before an emergency authority kicked in would not be accepted into the U.S., but would be detained while their asylum case was determined.

claimReviewed: The Emergency National Security Supplemental Appropriations Act “accepts 5,000 illegal immigrants a day.”

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): "Before I entered office, 100% of all new net jobs were going to migrant workers. ...
text:
"Before I entered office, 100% of all new net jobs were going to migrant workers. ... But since I took office, 100% of all net job creation has gone to American citizens."
These specific employment figures can mislead because the reported levels of native- and foreign-born workers are influenced by predetermined population estimates for 2025 that the Census Bureau calculated in 2024. The figures shouldn’t be used to make such comparisons, some experts have said.
licence: Metadane ClaimReview z publicznego feedu DataCommons Fact Check Markup (CC BY 4.0, autorzy ocen: wydawca); tylko teza, ocena, krótki fragment i link.
claimReviewed: "Before I entered office, 100% of all new net jobs were going to migrant workers. ... But since I took office, 100% of all net job creation has gone to American citizens."

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): President Joe Biden has "allowed an invasion to occur at our border, almost 10 million migrants have crossed into our country."
text:
President Joe Biden has "allowed an invasion to occur at our border, almost 10 million migrants have crossed into our country."
Government statistics show that in the initial processing of millions of encounters on the southwest border, 2.5 million people have been released into the U.S. and 2.8 million have been removed or expelled under Biden.

claimReviewed: President Joe Biden has "allowed an invasion to occur at our border, almost 10 million migrants have crossed into our country."

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “Russians are in Cuba firing missiles” as a warning to the U.S. about its resolve to win the war with Ukraine.
text:
“Russians are in Cuba firing missiles” as a warning to the U.S. about its resolve to win the war with Ukraine.
Russian warships on the way to an annual trip to Cuba conducted simulated missile drills in the Atlantic but did not fire live missiles from Cuba.

claimReviewed: “Russians are in Cuba firing missiles” as a warning to the U.S. about its resolve to win the war with Ukraine.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): On unaccompanied children who crossed the border, "88,000 children are missing under this administration. ...
text:
On unaccompanied children who crossed the border, "88,000 children are missing under this administration. ... And unfortunately, many of those children are dead."
In 2023, the New York Times reported that the Department of Health and Human Services was not able to get in contact with more than 85,000 children whom department officials had placed with relatives or other sponsors.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): "We have thousands of judges at the border. No other country has judges at the border. If somebody walks in, they walk them out.”
text:
"We have thousands of judges at the border. No other country has judges at the border. If somebody walks in, they walk them out.”
Many other countries accept refugees and allow them to stay in the country pending an asylum hearing in court, as is done in the U.S.

text:
Vice President Kamala Harris "was appointed border czar."
President Joe Biden assigned her to lead a group of actions intended to “address the root causes of migration from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras.”

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): "Look, [border] crossings are down compared to when Donald Trump left office.”
text:
"Look, [border] crossings are down compared to when Donald Trump left office.”
It’s true that the number of apprehensions of immigrants caught illegally crossing into the U.S. was lower in July and August than the last two months under Trump. But illegal immigration had soared under Biden.

text:
"I will follow the law" when it comes to allowing immigrants in the country illegally to apply for a driver’s license, to qualify for free tuition at universities or to be enrolled in free health care.
She has supported those positions in the past.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “A major factor in driving up housing costs was the colossal border invasion.”
text:
“A major factor in driving up housing costs was the colossal border invasion.”
Immigration does affect housing prices by increasing demand, but economists told us the main causes of higher prices in recent years were low mortgage interest rates that fueled demand, a subsequent rise in interest rates, and a low housing supply dating to the Great Recession in 2007 to 2009.

claimReviewed: “A major factor in driving up housing costs was the colossal border invasion.”

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): "There are ... 13,000 illegal immigrant murderers" in the U.S. "because [Vice President] Kamala Harris let them in this country."
text:
"There are ... 13,000 illegal immigrant murderers" in the U.S. "because [Vice President] Kamala Harris let them in this country."
The “vast majority” of the 13,099 entered the U.S. and had their custody status determined before the Biden administration, according to the Department of Homeland Security. They also gained entry legally and illegally.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): The U.S. has given Ukraine “$350 billion” for the war with Russia gave “$200 billion more than Europe.”
text:
The U.S. has given Ukraine “$350 billion” for the war with Russia gave “$200 billion more than Europe.”
Since 2022, Congress has appropriated about $174.2 billion in aid for Ukraine, according to a report by the Congressional Research Service. Europe outpaces the U.S., not the other way around, according to the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.

claimReviewed: The U.S. has given Ukraine “$350 billion” for the war with Russia gave “$200 billion more than Europe.”

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): Vice President Kamala Harris has "unleashed an army of migrant gangs. They're waging a campaign of violence and terror against our citizens
text:
Vice President Kamala Harris has "unleashed an army of migrant gangs. They're waging a campaign of violence and terror against our citizens like we've never suffered before."
There have been some high-profile crimes committed by immigrants who are in the country illegally, but there’s no evidence of a wave of what Trump has called “migrant crime” in the existing data, experts have said.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “The flow of deadly fentanyl across our border is down by a record 56% in one year.”
text:
“The flow of deadly fentanyl across our border is down by a record 56% in one year.”
Experts who study drug flow and policy have told us before that it’s not possible to know how much more or less of an illicit drug is getting into the U.S.

text:
Border crossings have created "flat-out economic warfare on African American and Hispanic American families and workers. These people are taking the jobs of African Americans, they’re taking the jobs of Hispanic Americans. ... Unions are being absolutely slaughtered."
Employment and union membership data show no evidence of that.

title: FactCheck.org (Annenberg Public Policy Center): “We paid for, in my opinion, 100% of NATO because they weren’t paying their bills.”
text:
“We paid for, in my opinion, 100% of NATO because they weren’t paying their bills.”
In terms of direct costs, the U.S., since January, pays about 15% of NATO’s “common-funded budgets." Trump for years has wrongly described what the U.S. willingly spends on its own defense budget as funding for NATO.

text:
Hunter Biden’s payments from the Ukrainian oil and gas company Burisma Holdings ended with the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Hunter left the Burisma board back in 2019 — almost three years before the war in Ukraine began.

text:
“Border encounters have dropped over 50%” and that “there are fewer border crossings today than when Donald Trump left office.”
Apprehensions of those trying to cross the southern border illegally plummeted in July, but illegal border crossings skyrocketed for most of Biden’s presidency.

text:
Referring to immigrants in a southwestern Ohio city, “In Springfield, they’re eating the dogs, the people that came in, they’re eating the cats. They’re eating, they’re eating the pets of the people that live there.”

The military equipment shown in the video was being prepared for its return to the U.S., not for shipment to Ukraine.
